Read-only investigation in the treams-rs repository (integration checkout treams-rs at d95280b (condensed into 8251007), venv .venv; the venv's python imports treams_rs from python with the current debug extension). Do NOT edit, commit or push anything in treams-rs, scratch: lanes/* or r4-tooling. Write scratch files only under legendre/. Keep CPU use low: run with taskset -c 3 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.

Report from another session (verify, do not assume it is right): tests/special/test_fractional_legendre.py::test_real_degree_reference_and_advect failed in a lane from a saved Hypothesis example: label=(20,11), fraction=0.0625, x=-0.875; relative error 1.4e-8 against rtol 5e-10. It passed in the integration checks with a fresh Hypothesis database.

Tasks:

  1. Read the test and find what it compares (implementation vs a reference: mpmath? scipy? a closed form?) and with which tolerance rule.
  2. Reproduce the exact failing input deterministically (call the functions directly with those values; also run the test with that example forced, e.g. via hypothesis @example in a scratch copy of the test outside the repo, or by calling the test body). Report the computed value, the reference value, and a high-precision value (mpmath with mp.dps = 50) to decide which side is wrong.
  3. Find the cause: is the implementation inaccurate at this (degree, order, x) (e.g. cancellation in a recurrence, a branch near x = -1, a hypergeometric series), is the reference inaccurate, or is the tolerance unrealistic for this region? Name files and line numbers (Rust in crates/treams-core/src/special/ and the Python wrappers).
  4. Scan nearby inputs (degree 20 + fraction in [0, 1), order 0..20, x in [-1, 1]) with a modest grid (keep it under 2 minutes of CPU) and report the worst relative error against mpmath, and where it occurs, so we know whether this is one point or a region.
  5. Check whether upstream treams (scratch: treams, importable as treams if installed) has the same function and how accurate it is at the same input.
  6. Recommend: (a) a fix in the implementation (describe it, and whether it would change any recorded result: check gates/current/{battery.py,uf_dump.py} for cases with fractional degrees), or (b) a test tolerance change with a stated justification, or (c) both. Remember the round rule: no numerical changes unless the owner approves, so state clearly whether the implementation is actually wrong (worse than a reasonable accuracy for double precision) or the test is too strict. Return a concise report with numbers, cause (file:line), the scan result, and the recommendation.

Fractional Legendre failure: the reference is wrong, not treams_rs

The failure is real and reproduces deterministically. The other session's description is right except for one thing: it is the reference value that is off by 1.4e-8. The treams_rs result agrees with mpmath to 5e-14.

I edited nothing in the repo (git status is clean). Scratch files are under legendre/.

1. What the test compares

  • The comparison is at tests/special/test_fractional_legendre.py:18-36: special.lpmv(order, degree, x) against oracle.lpmv (upstream treams.special, version 0.4.5).
  • Tolerance: rtol=5e-10, atol=2e-11*(1+|value|). That works out to a relative tolerance of about 5.2e-10.
  • Domain: degree_order(2, 20, margin=1) (degree n from 2 to 20, |m| ≤ n−1), fraction in [0.05, 0.95], x in [−0.9, 0.9].
  • For real x the reference is just SciPy. scratch: treams/src/treams/special/_waves.pyx:78-85 calls scipy.special.cython_special.lpmv (SciPy 1.16.3 here); _ufuncs.pyx:458-466 documents this.

2. Reproduction at m=11, ν=20.0625, x=−0.875

Source Value Relative error vs mpmath
mpmath, legenp(type=2), dps=50 412007810333.48649566436… —
treams_rs 412007810333.4654 5.1e-14
reference (treams 0.4.5 = SciPy lpmv) 412007816248.8 1.4357e-8
  • I ran a copy of the test with @example(label=(20,11), fraction=0.0625, x=-0.875) and the database disabled (forced/test_forced.py). It fails with "Max relative difference 1.43573359e-08", matching the report.
  • The gradient half of the test body passes at this input. The native derivative is within 1.3e-15 of mpmath.
  • The input is not badly conditioned. Sensitivity to x is about 1.5e3 and to the degree about 1.3e4 (κ_x = 1548, κ_ν = 1.33e4 in condition-number terms). In double precision that means a good algorithm should reach about 1.65e-12.
    • treams_rs is at about 0.03× that limit.
    • SciPy is about 8,700× over it.

3. Cause

SciPy (the reference) has two defects:

  • Unstable degree recursion. SciPy's specfun::lpmv evaluates two starting values at degrees v0+|m| and v0+|m|+1, then steps the degree upward at fixed m. The starting values are accurate (8e-15 and 1e-14). The error then grows along the way:

    Degree 13.0625 15.0625 20.0625
    SciPy relative error 1.5e-13 4.0e-12 1.4e-8
    • mpmath shows that a perturbation of a starting value is amplified 7.8e5 times.
    • The target degree sits next to a sign change of P along the degree: |P| goes from 5.3e12 at 19.0625 to 4.1e11 at 20.0625. Meanwhile the other solution of the recursion (Q) keeps growing, from 1.3e13 to 1.4e14. So each step cancels.
    • Even with correctly rounded starting values, the recursion in double precision gives 6.5e-11.

  • Series cut off at 100 terms. For x ≥ −0.35, SciPy sums a series that it stops after 100 terms. At x=−0.35, ν=19.25, m=19 this alone gives 5.1e-8 (with 200 terms: 1.3e-15). This defect causes most of SciPy's failures for x in [−0.35, 0).

treams_rs avoids both:

  • Call path: python/treams_rs/special.py:164-188 → crates/treams-core/src/special/legendre.rs:194-201 → ferrers.rs factor (lines 170-230) → regular_factor (119-155).
  • This input: for x < −0.35, |m| ≥ 2, ν > |m|+1 and a degree not within 1e-8 of an integer, it recurses in the order m instead of the degree (ferrers.rs:121-136). That path is stable.
  • Elsewhere: the SciPy-style degree recursion remains at ferrers.rs:140-154. The series in base_factor allows 200 terms (ferrers.rs:51).

4. Scan

  • Grid: degree 20+f with 30 fractions (0, 1e-12, 1e-9, 1e-6, 1e-3, …, 0.999, 1−1e-6), 88 values of x in (−1, 1] including ±0.999999, and orders −20 to 20. That is 107,010 points and took about 20 s of CPU.
  • Reference: mpmath at 50 digits. I checked it against direct 80-digit legenp at 140 points, including the edges and the worst points; the worst disagreement was 9.3e-17.
Region treams_rs worst treams_rs points > 5e-10 SciPy worst SciPy points > 5e-10
Test domain (56,940 points) 2.6e-11 0 2.9e-7 430
Whole grid 9.4e-4 (near a zero) 117 about 1e3 4,569
Integer degree only (f=0) 1.1e-10 0 1.1e-10 0
  • treams_rs in the test domain: the worst is at f=0.6, x=−0.775, m=−11. That point sits near a zero of P, where even a perfect algorithm can only promise about 2e-10; treams_rs is at 0.13× that.
  • treams_rs over the whole grid: the 9.4e-4 is at f=1e-12, x=0, m=±17, a value that is almost exactly zero (P^17_20(0) = 0 for the integer degree, so it is extremely sensitive to the degree). SciPy has the identical error there. All 117 points above 5e-10 are near-integer degrees (f ≤ 1e-6) or such zeros. Every worst case I checked was within the double-precision limit for that point (0.0004 to 0.55× of it).
  • Integer degree (f=0): the 1.1e-10 is at x=−0.999999, m=20, and comes from rounding of x itself. treams_rs and SciPy are identical there.
  • SciPy in the test domain is a region, not a point: failures occur for |m| ≥ 10 on this grid, with x from −0.9 to −0.25. In a random sample over all degrees they appear for |m| 7–19, degree 13–20 and x up to 0.46.
  • How often the test trips: 0.037% of uniform random examples fail. I checked 74 of the failures against mpmath; every one is SciPy's error (treams_rs worst there 1.7e-11). With Hypothesis's real example distribution, 2 of 300 seeded 60-example runs (0.7%) produce a failing example. The fixed-seed (CI-style) run does not. Once a lane finds one, its example database replays it. That explains why the lane failed and the fresh-database integration check passed.

5. Upstream treams

Upstream has the same function, treams.special.lpmv, and for real x it is exactly SciPy's lpmv. At this input it gives 412007816248.8, the same 1.44e-8 error. Upstream has nothing more accurate.

6. Recommendation: (b), change the test only

treams_rs is not wrong. It is within the double-precision limit everywhere I scanned and 20× under the test tolerance in the test's domain. The test is effectively measuring SciPy's error. No numerical change is warranted.

  • No implementation fix. Nothing recorded would change. The recorded fractional-degree cases are gates/current/battery.py:595-620 (special_legendre_fractional_degree) and uf_dump.py:335-341 (degree 2.5); they stay valid. Making treams_rs agree with SciPy would make it less accurate.
  • Test change (for the owner to approve):
    • Replace oracle.lpmv in this property with float(mpmath.legenp(degree, order, x, type=2)) at mp.dps = 30. The sign convention matches. It costs about 7 ms per call, under 0.5 s for 60 examples.
    • Import it with pytest.importorskip("mpmath", ...) as tests/scripts/test_qualify_references.py:17 does. mpmath is already in the dev dependencies.
    • Keep rtol=5e-10 and the current atol. Do not tighten much: near zeros of P in this domain, the double-precision limit itself reaches about 2e-10.
    • Add @example(label=(20, 11), fraction=0.0625, x=-0.875) as a regression case.
    • If you want to keep a comparison against upstream treams, make it a separate check with rtol of about 1e-6. Justify it in a comment by SciPy's degree recursion and 100-term cut-off (worst seen in the domain: 2.9e-7).
  • Not recommended: only loosening the SciPy comparison to 1e-6 (the test would lose 3–4 orders of sensitivity), or shrinking the domain. Clearing the lane's Hypothesis database would only hide the failure until the test changes.

Scratch scripts in legendre/: scan.py, analyze.py and analyze2.py (the scan), mech.py (cause), cond.py and cond2.py (sensitivity), mc.py and hyprate.py (failure rate).
